name: a pothole made of two small eroded basins joined by a narrow neck, lying diagonally, with dark dirt floors darker than the road, shadowed far walls, a thin lit near inner wall, broken lighter near rims and a couple of loose fragments; transparent decal on old asphalt

surfaces.part: asphalt patch with brown dirt border and potholes, seen from directly above

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a uniform 48-wide square on all 48 rows. The interior is gray asphalt speckled with lighter and darker patches, framed by a brown dirt border. The dark brown pothole basins sit around rows 19-30 with a few loose fragments. The column scans show only flat texture bands at x=12 and x=35, with no front-edge line, eave shadow or vertical front face. The thin dark and light lines at rows 44-47 are part of the border outline, not a front face. This is a flat floor decal seen from above, which matches the flat kind, and it has no front face of 3 or more rows.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's edge pixels are only 5% neutral, so the dark brown-tinted rim reads as a material-tone outline, which is good. The measured tones per tile (7) match the paving reference, and near-flat coverage is 14% against 0% for both references. The candidate has only 9 distinct colours in total, so its ramps are shallow: about 4 steps on the asphalt and 3-4 on the pothole. The asphalt shows sparse speckle with some flat patches. The pothole is small and the two basins are hard to read, with no clear thin lit near wall, per-fragment shading or broken-rim detail. Beodeul paving shades every stone individually across 5-6 steps with highlight edges. Next to it the candidate looks flatter and less crafted, so I fail it because of the shallow ramps and residual flat fills rather than the measured tone count alone.
